requirements:
Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with `rustc --edition 2024`, using std only. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences. Do not use inner attributes or inner documentation comments.

All API types, fields, variants, and functions below must be public. Types must derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq; Section and Op, where present, must also derive Copy. The evaluator compiles the source as a test crate using `rustc --test --edition 2024`; no main function is needed.

Parse the three core components as u64. Do not trim input. Only ASCII digits are valid in a core component; do not accept signs, a v prefix, or whitespace. Empty entire input gives EmptyInput. Otherwise split the core on literal dots, preserving empty components: before inspecting components, require exactly three components or give ComponentCount { found: number_of_components }. Then inspect components in order major (index 0), minor (1), patch (2). Within each component check, in this order: empty => EmptyComponent; first non-ASCII-digit => InvalidDigit (offset is its zero-based UTF-8 BYTE offset within this component); more than one digit starting with zero => LeadingZero; value above u64::MAX => Overflow. Return the first error in this order. A single zero is valid; u64::MAX is valid. All component error indices are zero based. Core numeric validation precedes all identifier validation.

Exact public API (include the derives specified above):
```rust
pub struct Version { pub major: u64, pub minor: u64, pub patch: u64 }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ParseError {
    EmptyInput,
    ComponentCount { found: usize },
    EmptyComponent { index: usize },
    InvalidDigit { index: usize, offset: usize },
    LeadingZero { index: usize },
    Overflow { index: usize },

}
pub fn parse_version(input: &str) -> Result<Version, ParseError>;
```

The entire input is the core; prerelease and build suffixes are not supported in this level and are rejected by the core digit rules.
